text: The key distinction between Σ(x:A).P(x) and ∥Σ(x:A).P(x)∥ is:
choices: the former gives an explicit witness; the latter gives mere existence (no choice of witness)
the latter is a set; the former may not be
the former is a proposition; the latter is not
explanation: Σ(x:A).P(x) = 'there exists x with P(x) AND we know which x'. ∥Σ(x:A).P(x)∥ = 'merely there exists'.
